sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Sampson County?
sections.html:
The Sampson County Tax Office collects county, fire district and school district taxes. It is also currently collecting for the municipalities of Clinton, Autryville, Harrells, Newton Grove, Salemburg, Turkey and Garland, so one bill can cover several levies.

Real estate and personal property bills are mailed in July or August. Bills for registered motor vehicles come from the state Division of Motor Vehicles instead of the county. The tax office can be reached at (910) 592-8146, and mail goes to PO Box 1082, Clinton, NC 28329.

The county runs an online property record search and a tax bill search and payment site. A seller can use them to confirm the parcel, owner of record and balance before a listing goes live.

sections.h2: When are Sampson County property taxes due, and what happens if they are late?
sections.html:
Real and personal property taxes are due September 1. The county gives a 2 percent discount on real and personal property if paid by August 31, or postmarked by then, with the date moved to the next business day when August 31 falls on a weekend.

  • Taxes become delinquent if not paid by January 5, and payments before that date are interest free.
  • Unpaid balances then carry 2 percent interest for January and an additional three-quarters of one percent for each month after.
  • Partial payments are accepted until the account becomes delinquent.
  • Mailed payments count as received on the postmark date.

Unpaid real estate parcels are advertised in the local newspaper in the owner's name, usually in the first week of April, and the advertising costs become part of the tax lien. Collection steps listed by the county include wage garnishment, bank attachment, seizure and sale, debt setoff and foreclosure.

sections.html:

Your total depends on which district and town the parcel sits in. A parcel's bill adds the county-wide rate to the school, fire and municipal figures that apply to it.

sections.h2: How is real estate valued in Sampson County?
sections.html:
Sampson County assessed values reflect market value as of January 1, 2024, and they stay in effect until the next county-wide revaluation. The county says revaluation happens every eight years and names 2028 as the next one. State law sets the eight-year cycle (G.S. 105-286).

Because the date is fixed, market swings after the valuation date cannot be considered in an appeal. If your house has sold for far more or less since 2024, that fact alone does not change the assessed figure. Physical facts as of the valuation date, such as a wrong square footage or a listed building that no longer stands, are the stronger grounds for a review.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Sampson County property value?
sections.html:
You can appeal real estate values beginning January 1 each year, and the deadline is the day the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns, which the county says is usually early May. If you were notified of a changed value only after the board adjourned, the stated deadline is December 31.

  • Informal review: available when the assessed value changed since the prior bill and this is your first notice. Call (910) 592-8146 or write to Sampson County Tax Department, Attention: Real Estate Appeal, PO Box 1082, Clinton, NC 28329.
  • Formal appeal: request a Board of Equalization and Review application by phone. The county commissioners serve as that board, and the application must arrive before it adjourns.
  • Next level: the North Carolina Property Tax Commission, with an application filed within 30 days after the board mails its decision.

Personal property appeals have their own 30 day windows, and vehicle appeals must be postmarked within 30 days of the due date printed on the notice. Registered vehicles are valued at retail level, so bring dealer paperwork and condition photos instead of internet book values.

sections.h2: What tax relief exists for Sampson County homeowners?
sections.html:
North Carolina offers three relief programs, and an owner may receive only one. The application is Form AV-9, filed with the county assessor rather than the state, and it must be accepted through June 1 before the tax year.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50 percent of the appraised value of a permanent residence, for owners at least 65 or totally and permanently disabled. The state's printed income limit is $38,800 for 2026 (G.S. 105-277.1).
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • Circuit breaker: taxes capped at 4.0 percent of income up to the limit and 5.0 percent between the limit and 150 percent of it, with the excess deferred (G.S. 105-277.1B).

Deferred circuit breaker taxes for the preceding three years come due if the owner transfers the property, dies, or stops using it as a permanent residence. A sale of the house triggers that bill, so ask the tax office for the amount before closing.

sections.h2: How should I handle Sampson County property tax when I sell a house?
sections.html:
Pay or settle the tax at closing through your closing attorney. The lien for county tax attaches as of the listing date, so a buyer's title company will want the year's balance cleared or prorated (G.S. 105-355). Ask the Sampson County Tax Office for a payoff figure on every parcel that is part of the sale.

If the taxes were already advertised in April, the advertising costs are part of the lien and must be paid too. If a parcel goes to foreclosure, the sale is an auction at the courthouse door, and a person who redeems before confirmation pays the taxes plus penalties, interest and costs (G.S. 105-374).

The register of deeds records the deed after closing, and the seller pays the excise tax of $1.00 for each $500 of value. Seller and buyer can split the year's tax in the contract, so write the proration terms down.

faqs.q: When are Sampson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1. The county gives a 2 percent discount if paid or postmarked by August 31. Taxes are delinquent after January 5, and interest begins then at 2 percent for January and three-quarters of one percent monthly after.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Sampson County real estate value?
faqs.a: Start an informal review by calling (910) 592-8146 if your value changed, or request a Board of Equalization and Review application. The county says the deadline is when the board adjourns, usually early May.

faqs.q: When is the next Sampson County revaluation?
faqs.a: The county names 2028. Current assessed values reflect market value as of January 1, 2024, and stay in effect until then.

faqs.q: Where do I mail a Sampson County tax appeal?
faqs.a: Real estate and personal property appeals go to the tax office at PO Box 1082, Clinton, NC 28329, marked for the right appeal type. Vehicle appeals can also be emailed, with the address listed on the county's appeal page.

faqs.q: Can I claim homestead relief in Sampson County and a veteran exclusion together?
faqs.a: No. An owner may receive benefit from only one of the three state programs. File Form AV-9 with the county tax assessor and choose the program that fits your situation.
